draft.title: Reflection, refraction and absorption
card: Reflection
Light bounces off a surface. A smooth, shiny surface such as a mirror reflects light in a clear, regular way, so we see an image.
Refraction
Light bends when it passes from one material into another, such as from air into water. This happens because light changes speed in the new material.
Absorption
A surface takes in some of the light that hits it and changes its energy, often into heat. Dark surfaces absorb more light than light-coloured ones.
One surface can do more than one of these. Light hitting a pond is partly reflected, partly absorbed and partly refracted as it enters the water.
draft.remember: Reflection bounces light, refraction bends it, and absorption takes it in.

a.q: A straw in a glass of water looks bent at the water's surface. Which process causes this?
opts: Refraction
Reflection
Absorption
Emission
a.why: Light bends as it passes between water and air, which changes how the straw looks. Reflection is light bouncing off a surface, which does not bend the path of light through a material.
a.clue: Think about light moving from one material into another.

b.q: Liam wears a black shirt and a white shirt on a sunny day. Why does the black shirt feel hotter?
opts: It absorbs more light and changes it to heat
It reflects more light and so gains more heat
It refracts more light into the skin
It absorbs less light than the white shirt
b.why: Dark surfaces take in more of the light that hits them, and that energy becomes heat. The tempting idea that it reflects more is wrong: the white shirt reflects more light, so it stays cooler.
b.clue: Which colour takes in more light, and where does that energy go?

b.best: It absorbs more light and changes it to heat

problems.detail: "Liam wears a black shirt and a white shirt on a sunny day" reads as if he wears both at once, perhaps layered. It should say he wears them on different days, or compare two people, so the comparison is clear.
